map.体重法：单次剂量 = 体重(kg) × 每公斤剂量(mg/kg)，日剂量 = 单: Weight method: dose per administration = weight (kg) × dose per kg (mg/kg), daily dose = dose per administration × doses per day. Body surface area method: BSA (m²) = √(height (cm) × weight (kg) ÷ 3600) (Mosteller formula), dose per administration = BSA × dose per m² (mg/m²), daily dose = single dose × times. A warning is given when the daily dose exceeds the drug's maxDay.
map.60 kg、170 cm、30 岁，对乙酰氨基酚按体重法 10 mg/kg、每日: 60 kg, 170 cm, age 30, paracetamol by weight at 10 mg/kg once daily: single dose = 60 × 10 = 600.0 mg, daily dose = 600.0 mg, below the drug's maximum daily dose of 4000 mg. The same patient switched to the body surface area method (10 mg/m²): BSA = √(170 × 60 ÷ 3600) = √2.8333 ≈ 1.68 m², single dose = 1.68 × 10 ≈ 16.8 mg, daily dose 16.8 mg. The gap in magnitude between the two methods shows the point: the dosing basis (mg/kg or mg/m²) must strictly follow the label and the two are not interchangeable — 10 mg/kg by weight for adults differs from 10 mg/m² by body surface area by about a factor of 35.
map.什么时候该用体表面积而不是体重？: When should body surface area be used instead of body weight?
map.细胞毒类抗肿瘤药、部分免疫抑制剂与儿科专用药多以 mg/m² 处方，因为体表面积: Cytotoxic antitumour drugs, some immunosuppressants and paediatric-specific drugs are commonly prescribed in mg/m², because body surface area correlates more strongly with basal metabolic rate, liver and kidney function and drug clearance than body weight does, which reduces dose deviation in obese or cachectic patients. Ordinary anti-infectives and antipyretic analgesics are still dosed in mg/kg or at a fixed dose. The basis of dosing is always whatever the label states.

map.，在常规体型范围内与 Du Bois 结果相差通常小于 1%-2%，便于床旁手算: ; within normal body sizes the difference from the Du Bois result is usually below 1%-2%, which makes bedside hand calculation easy. For extreme body sizes (severe obesity, severe emaciation, extensive oedema) use a measured or more precise formula.

BSA method: BSA(m²) = √(height (cm) × weight (kg) ÷ 3600) (Mosteller formula), single dose = BSA × dose per square meter (mg/m²), daily dose = single dose × doses. The two bases must be chosen according to the drug label; never treat an mg/m² value as mg/kg and multiply by weight. This page automatically uses the BSA method for BSA-based drugs. When the daily dose exceeds the drug maxDay, an over-limit warning is shown.
